name: Coinbase BTC/USD effective and realized spread
description: At each Coinbase BTC/USD trade, effective_spread_bps = 2 * side_sign * (trade_price - midpoint) / midpoint expressed in basis points, where midpoint is the freshest Coinbase top-of-book midpoint at or before the trade's event time and side_sign is +1 for a buyer-aggressor and -1 for a seller-aggressor. The paired realized_spread_bps applies the same formula against the prevailing midpoint at trade_time plus realized_horizon_ms — the freshest Coinbase midpoint at or before that horizon (the midpoint is a step function, so this is the textbook TAQ mid at t plus horizon). Effective spread is not ready until a Coinbase midpoint has been observed, and a trade with no prevailing midpoint has no defined spread and enqueues no realized measurement. Realized spread stays awaiting_horizon until an event strictly past the horizon is observed; resolution then uses the prevailing at-or-before-horizon midpoint (the pre-trade midpoint when none arrived within the horizon), and a later midpoint never retroactively changes a resolved value. The published reading is the most recent resolved measurement when one exists, otherwise the most recent priced trade still awaiting its horizon. Every state-dependent field is always present: while a measurement is awaiting_horizon, realized_present is false and realized_spread_bps and midpoint_at_horizon carry the explicit 0 sentinel, so a ready update never omits a declared field. No value is ever fabricated. These are textbook TAQ execution-cost measures. realized_horizon_ms defaults to 5000. This identity is single-venue by construction: the measurement compares one venue's own trades and book against each other, so it reads only Coinbase inputs and is ready whenever the Coinbase book-and-trade join is fresh, independently of the other adopted spot venue. No blended `btc.external.*` variant of this measurement is published: a cross-venue form would have to rule which venue's book prices another venue's trade, and that ruling is deferred pending evidence (ADR 0023 amendment and ADR 0024, both 2026-09-02). Decimal outputs are rounded to eight places using round-half-to-even.
